questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kiribati?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kiribati article.

questions.proof: Its capital is South Tarawa, on the Tarawa atoll.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kiribati?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kiribati on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Kiribati article.

questions.proof: Kiribati signed a "Treaty of Friendship and Territorial Sovereignty" (also called the "Treaty of Tarawa") with the United States in 1979.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Kiribati?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kiribati article.

questions.proof: The official languages of Kiribati are English and Gilbertese.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1892, the Gilbert Islands became a British protectorate with the Ellice Islands (now known as _____), together called Gilbert and Ellice Islands.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “together”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kiribati article.

questions.proof: In 1892, the Gilbert Islands became a British protectorate with the Ellice Islands (now known as Tuvalu), together called Gilbert and Ellice Islands.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Kiribati became an independent republic in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kiribati article.

questions.proof: Kiribati became an independent republic in 1979.
